arms.predicted: The paper's best-fit ITL = alpha/(1-rate*w) formula will achieve R-squared below 0.95 for BOTH AL and AD modes across the full rate range (5-150 req/s), while a simple linear fit ITL = a + b*rate will achieve R-squared above 0.95 for both modes. The formula's failure is due to a shape mismatch: data is approximately linear (concave) while 1/(1-rho) is convex. Additionally, w_AL will be strictly larger than w_AD.

discrepancy_analysis: All three arms CONFIRMED. The paper's ITL=alpha/(1-rho) formula is accurate in the steady-state regime (rates 5-20, MAPE < 0.1%) but fails quantitatively at high rates due to finite-horizon transient effects — the 300-request simulation never reaches steady-state batch size at rates >= 60 req/s. A simple linear fit (R²>0.975) outperforms the best-fit formula (R²<0.95) across the full 5-150 req/s range. The overprediction is strictly monotone increasing with rate, confirming the transient mechanism. Two-point-calibrated formula parameters confirm w_AL>w_AD (0.004707 vs 0.003685), consistent with the paper's prediction that local processing adds more per-request work than disaggregated decode-only processing.
